subject: knitr with beamer with figure environment: vertical spacing

messages.author: 074af49060f6d28c
messages.subject: knitr with beamer with figure environment: vertical spacing
parts:
I have a standard beamer theme (default with minor adjustments) and most of my frames contain a single figure with a caption and frametitle but no other text. Too much space is inserted above and below the figure.

Any idea what is causing this?

Thanks!

Here is a typical frame: (Note: the code above and below the lines of %%% is copied verbatim, including spacing)

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%% Frame Here %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\begin{frame}[label=Figure_1_1b]
\frametitle{Figure 1.1. The distribution of world output, 1700--2012}
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
<<'Figure_1_1b', out.width='1\\linewidth'>>=
load("data/df_1_1.Rda")  # load data from /data subdirectory
ggplot(data = df_1_1, aes(x = Year, y = value, group = variable, fill = variable)) + geom_area(position = 'stack', colour = gray, alpha = .4, show_guide = TRUE) + ylab("Share in world output (% of total)") + xlab(NULL) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(1700, 2012), breaks = seq(1700, 2020, by = 50)) + scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, breaks = seq(0, 1, by = .1)) + scale_fill_brewer(palette = fillPalette) + theme(legend.position = c(0.25, 0.75), legend.title = element_blank()) + guides(shape = guide_legend(ncol = 1), fill = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE))
@
\caption{Europe's GDP made 47 percent of world GDP in 1913, down to 25 percent in 2012.}
\end{figure}
\end{frame}
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%% Frame Here %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%

and here is the corresponding frame after being processed by knitr


%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%% Frame Here %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\begin{frame}[label=Figure_1_1b]
\frametitle{Figure 1.1. The distribution of world output, 1700--2012}
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\begin{knitrout}\footnotesize
\definecolor{shadecolor}{rgb}{0.969, 0.969, 0.969}\color{fgcolor}

{\centering \includegraphics[width=1\linewidth]{figures/bw/Figure_1_1b}

}



\end{knitrout}
\caption{Europe's GDP made 47 percent of world GDP in 1913, down to 25 percent in 2012.}
\end{figure}
\end{frame}
%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%% Frame Here %%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%


1. I have not been able to identify the source of the extra space above the figure.
2. the extra space below the figure is caused by the space above \end{knitrout}: 3 full lines inserted by knitr.

I am using the following workaround, but I would be interested in knowing the cause of the spaces: is it an incorrect or awkward design of my frames or something else?

The workaround to remove the excessive space:
\let\myfigure\figure
\let\endmyfigure\endfigure
\renewenvironment{figure}
  {\vspace{-4ex}\myfigure}
  {\endmyfigure\vspace{-4ex}}
